prompts.text: Which version of me do you remember which I rarely mention now?
Tell me about a moment you realised our friendship mattered beyond shared circumstances.
What have we learnt about handling unequal amounts of free time?
Keep a shared tradition unchanged or let it evolve with our present lives?
Our friendship deserves room for seasons when neither person is entertaining. How do we create it?
One of us achieves a goal the other still struggles towards. What would thoughtful celebration involve?
Which assumption about our friendship should we check rather than inherit from its beginning?
We sometimes retell the same memory for different reasons. What does our favourite shared story mean to you?
When do you feel I know your present life rather than only our history?
Describe a time you wanted my company but did not know how to ask.
What difference between our lives has helped you understand me better?
Our usual way of meeting no longer suits one person's budget. How would we change it gracefully?
Which subject do we handle better now than when we first became friends?
Friends need a way to express hurt without proving the friendship has failed. What would help us?
Hear an old memory I kept to myself or tell me a memory you think I forgot?
Tell me about a time our friendship gave you courage outside our friendship.
What do you enjoy about who we become around each other?
A familiar joke sometimes belongs to an earlier season. Which joke have we outgrown?
When have we made room for each other's changing priorities successfully?
One of us needs to leave an event while the other wants to stay. What would supportive independence look like?
Which part of my life would you like to hear more about without needing an invitation?
Describe a moment when you noticed I had changed before I noticed it myself.
Friendship should make asking for company easier than inventing an excuse to meet. How does this feel between us?
What would make our check-ins feel less like progress reports?
Revisit somewhere important to our friendship or create a new memory somewhere unfamiliar?
Which difference in our ambitions has required the most understanding?
We disagree about someone we both know. How would we protect independent relationships with that person?
Tell me about something I did which you understood differently much later.
Our friendship includes people who knew us at different times. What do those people miss about our connection?
When do you feel most free to be ordinary with me?
Friends should be able to say they feel left out without competing for a place. How do we make this possible?
What have we learnt from a plan which disappointed both of us?
Ask me for a practical favour or invite me to sit with an unresolved feeling?
Describe a time we handled a misunderstanding better than our younger selves would have.
Which pressure do we accidentally add when trying to encourage each other?
One of us wants a quieter friendship season without ending the connection. What would we need to discuss?
What do you wish I asked before assuming I understand your situation?
We might remember who initiated our friendship differently. What do you remember about its beginning?
Tell me about a moment you felt included in my life without being useful to me.
Being close friends does not make us responsible for every opinion the other person holds. Where are our limits?
Which quality of mine have you come to appreciate through seeing its difficult side?
Receive a detailed update less often or exchange brief glimpses of ordinary life regularly?
A mutual friend asks us to keep a disagreement secret from each other. What would feel fair?
What do you want our friendship to preserve as our daily lives change?
Describe a time I underestimated how much something mattered to you.
When has our friendship helped you question a harsh opinion of yourself?
We often notice a friend's visible achievements before their private adjustments. Which adjustment would you like me to recognise?
A friend deserves curiosity after a bad decision as well as before it. What does this involve for us?
Which part of being supported by me feels easiest to accept?
We both need support during the same week. How would we avoid treating care as a competition?
Tell me about a time you felt proud of me without mentioning it.
What do our disagreements reveal about the different things we try to protect?
Hear my honest first reaction or give me time to offer a more considered response?
What helps you trust my concern without feeling I am supervising you?
Our friendship should survive an honest change in taste. Which changes have been easiest to share?
A favourite activity becomes difficult for one of us because of health or energy. How would we stay connected?
We sometimes ask familiar questions because we do not know a friend's new questions. What occupies your thoughts lately?
Describe a time we enjoyed silence for different reasons.
Which small promise between us has carried more meaning than expected?
Plan one dependable meeting each month or leave room for spontaneous contact?
What would help you tell me I have misunderstood your enthusiasm?
Someone describes our friendship in a way neither of us recognises. What would you want to explain?
Friends should not need to become available immediately to prove they care. What signals of care work for us?
Tell me about an experience which showed you a strength in our friendship.
Which comparison with somebody else's friendship distracts us from what works here?
We sometimes keep a friend in an old role because it feels familiar. Which role should we reconsider?
What do you want me to remember when you say you need time alone?
Revisit an unresolved question together or agree it does not need resolving for us to stay close?
One of us changes their social circle. What would help the other avoid treating it as rejection?
Describe a time our friendship felt different in a good way.
What have I learnt about you by getting something wrong?
A friend is allowed to notice a change without knowing its cause. How should we ask about it?
What did watching me change my mind teach you about how I reach a decision?
Some friendship milestones have no date attached. What moment counts as a milestone for us?
Tell me about something you learnt about my values through watching me treat another person.
A shared project ends awkwardly. What would protect the friendship beyond the project?
What would make borrowing something from each other feel clearer and more comfortable?
Remember our funniest shared mistake or discuss what our hardest shared experience taught us?
When have I helped you feel less defined by a setback?
Friends should be able to celebrate progress at different speeds. What makes this difficult sometimes?
Describe a time I listened in a way you needed but had not requested.
Which limit in our friendship has become easier for you to understand?
One of us needs to cancel repeatedly for a genuine reason. How would we discuss the effect without questioning the reason?
We sometimes give a friend the advice our past self needed. How do we check whether it fits now?
What does being reliable to each other mean at our current stage of life?
Share an unfinished idea with me early or invite me in after you have found your direction?
Tell me about a time you understood my quiet support only afterwards.
Which kind of honesty between us has taken practice?
Our friendship should leave room for people we do not share. How do we protect this space?
We feel differently about posting a shared memory online. How should we decide what remains private?
What have we never needed to explain to each other, and why does it feel understood?
A friendship sometimes grows through seeing how a person repairs a small mistake. What repair do you remember?
Describe a moment you felt I trusted your judgement even though I chose differently.
Hear what I admire about your consistency or what I admire about your changes?
Which habit have we mistaken for a requirement of friendship?
Friends should not have to retell pain to keep receiving care. How do we remember what matters?
One of us becomes the organiser by default. What would a fairer arrangement look like?
What would help you say you need celebration rather than advice?
Tell me about a time being around me helped you feel more like yourself.
We sometimes measure closeness by the past. What present choice tells you we are still choosing this friendship?
What do you want to be able to ask me without rehearsing first?
Hear an honest concern privately now or discuss it once we both have more time?
A joke I enjoy makes you feel reduced to an old version of yourself. What should I hear?
Describe a friendship lesson we learnt without naming it at the time.
When do you feel I celebrate who you are rather than what you achieve?
A friendship is not automatically weaker because it becomes less public. What tells us it remains alive?
Which difference in how we handle stress deserves more understanding?
An old friend knows patterns a newer person might miss. How do we use this knowledge kindly?
Tell me about a time our friendship made a new place feel less unfamiliar.
We remember a hurtful conversation differently. What would let us acknowledge both experiences without erasing either?
What do you need from me when you are unsure whether your feelings make sense?
Receive comfort before a difficult decision or company while living with its consequences?
Friends sometimes need permission to ask an old question again. Which question has changed meaning for you?
What helps you tell me about a success without worrying it sounds like showing off?
Describe a time I took a small part of your life more seriously than expected.
We might agree on the facts of a shared experience and differ about its importance. Which experience illustrates this?
A mutual group assumes we always speak for each other. How would we protect our separate voices?
When have you felt understood by how I remembered something?
Friends need not turn every shared interest into a joint plan. What do you enjoy keeping separate?
Make a new memory during a practical errand or reserve time for an intentional catch-up?
Tell me about a moment you chose to be patient with a part of me you did not understand.
Which past expectation would you rewrite if our friendship began today?
One of us gives more advice than they receive. What might make the conversation more reciprocal?
A friend's growth sometimes changes what they ask from us. What do you ask from me differently now?
What does protecting my dignity look like when you disagree with my behaviour?
Supporting a friend should not require pretending a plan has no risks. How do we discuss risk kindly?
Describe a time one of us recognised the other needed a different sort of day.
Hear a friend say they missed you or hear how they have made room for seeing you?
When do you feel I allow your answer to surprise me?
Someone criticises me while I am absent. How would you balance fairness, loyalty and incomplete information?
We sometimes keep meeting in a setting which no longer suits either person. What setting would fit us now?
Which part of our friendship do you hope we never treat as automatic?
Tell me about learning something important from an ordinary conversation between us.
An honest friendship makes room for saying a particular kind of help is unhelpful. What would you like us to notice?
How do our different approaches to money affect shared plans emotionally?
Explain a changed boundary through a conversation or through a clear practical arrangement?
One of us wants to revisit a friendship ritual the other has outgrown. What would honour both meanings?
Describe a time you enjoyed seeing me become close to someone new.
What would make it easier to disagree about how we handled a shared situation?
Friends sometimes notice fatigue before the person names it. What response feels caring to you?
We should be able to change plans without making someone prove they are exhausted enough. What makes this fair?
Which form of attention from me helps you slow down?
A plan important to you matters less to me. How could I participate honestly without dismissing it?
Tell me about a time you wanted to thank me but did not find the right moment.
Discuss a friendship concern during an ordinary walk or arrange a dedicated conversation?
What do you appreciate about the differences between how we express affection?
We sometimes recognise a turning point only when looking back together. What turning point would you name?
A friend deserves more than a permanent label as the strong one. Which labels should we retire?
What would let our friendship feel spacious without becoming distant?
One of us says they miss how things used to be. What part of the past would be worth identifying precisely?
Describe a time our friendship helped you attempt something outside your usual role.
When have I made a difficult choice feel less lonely without deciding it for you?
Hear about my present uncertainty or learn something I have recently become certain about?
Our friendship should hold room for boredom without treating it as a problem. What makes ordinary company enough?
A friendship might feel balanced across years rather than weeks. How do we recognise this without keeping score?
Which question have you wanted to ask about how I experience our friendship?
Tell me about a time you felt my support continue after a conversation ended.
One of us avoids mentioning a problem to protect a happy occasion. When should we return to it?
What helps you trust a promise from me after circumstances change?
Friends sometimes mistake shared history for a shared interpretation of it. What memory should we hear from each other anew?
Offer encouragement publicly or protect a friend's privacy while they find their footing?
We sometimes notice a friend's need for recognition only after they stop contributing. What should we notice earlier?
Describe a time you felt our friendship had room for your mixed feelings about me.
Which kind of misunderstanding do we now recognise before it grows?
We give different meanings to a missed message. What expectations should we compare?
Our friendship need not justify its value through dramatic moments. What makes it valuable on an ordinary week?
What do you want me to understand about the way you process a difficult conversation afterwards?
Revisit a shared success or recognise something difficult we handled with little acknowledgment?
Tell me about a time I surprised you by asking instead of assuming.
A friend's honest limit offers information about their life. What limit of mine helped you understand me?
Which part of our friendship has become simpler as we have become more honest?
A new responsibility reduces the time one of us has for everyone. How could our friendship adapt without guilt?
Friends should be able to want different futures without turning them into competing arguments. How do we protect this?
Describe a moment when you felt I understood your intention and still helped you see an effect.
What have you learnt about receiving care from how we support one another?
Ask me to help you think something through or ask me to distract you for a while?
We sometimes remember a friend's old worries longer than their new confidence. What confidence should I recognise in you?
One of us is quiet during a shared celebration. How would the other check in without demanding a different mood?
What would you like our friendship to make easier during an uncertain year?
Tell me about a time you felt chosen in our friendship without anyone making a grand statement.
Trust between friends includes believing an honest 'I cannot take this on.' What helps us hear it?
Which part of my perspective do you understand more sympathetically now?
Share a small daily concern now or save it until we have time for a fuller conversation?
An occasion important to one of us clashes with a commitment important to the other. What would respectful negotiation involve?
Describe a time we stayed connected without knowing how to solve the problem between us.
Friends sometimes develop shared shorthand which hides changing meanings. Which familiar phrase should we explain again?
What does letting our friendship grow ask you to release from its earlier form?
A friendship needs curiosity about a person's choices, not permission over them. How do we preserve this difference?
Hear what I learnt from you recently or tell me something I have helped you reconsider?
Tell me about a time our friendship felt stronger because we allowed a difference to remain.
Which response from me makes a difficult day feel more manageable?
One of us worries a favour has created a debt. What would make the intention clear?
An old friend sometimes witnesses growth the person struggles to believe. What growth would you like me to reflect back?
Care between friends should survive an honest conversation about imbalance. What would make this conversation fair?
What would you like us to learn about each other during the next year?
Protect time for a familiar friendship ritual or make room for a new way of staying close?
We both think we have been giving the other space. How would we check whether either person feels neglected?
Describe a time you felt safe being less certain around me than you were in public.
Our friendship contains more than either person's account of it. What would you add to my version?
What deserves more care between us now, even if it once took care of itself?
